answer: Cross-Epoch Identity Continuity Scoring. Each identity carries a behavioural fingerprint (timing, task mix, response patterns) compared across epochs; large unexplained shifts trigger demotion. An attacker splitting into many identities must maintain each one's consistency separately across every epoch, multiplying upkeep work per identity. A sudden wander in style flags the clone, and any gale of new registrations inherits low trust until it survives several epochs. Growth is slow, like a garden: trust compounds only through sustained, matching behaviour,
